title: Quiz 6 — spin-space-group numbers, magnon–phonon coupling, quasi-harmonic & anharmonic hulls

questions.question: What does the OSSG number of Chen et al. (2024) add to SymPhase's own collinear SSG label?

options.b: a standard number for every order, including coplanar and non-coplanar ones

questions.explanation: SymPhase numbers collinear SSGs via the C2⊥→T black-and-white group; FindSpinGroup gives the four-index OSSG for any order.

questions.question: Hands-on: the OSSG index of Mn3Sn (all-in coplanar 120° order, examples/vasp/Mn3Sn_allin) is …
questions.explanation: Coplanar ('P' suffix), G0 = P6_3/mmc (194), spin point group 6/mmm.

questions.question: Hands-on: the OSSG index of the altermagnet MnTe is …
questions.explanation: Collinear ('L'), spin point group ∞/mm; the same index appears in the FindSpinGroup documentation.

questions.question: Hands-on: which suffix does the non-coplanar skyrmion crystal of tutorial 12 get (OSSG 191.6.1.2)?
questions.explanation: Collinear orders end in L, coplanar in P; a non-coplanar order has a trivial spin-only group and no suffix.

questions.question: Why does SymPhase compare the MSG derived by FindSpinGroup with its own spglib result?

options.b: as an independent consistency check of moments, tolerances and frames

questions.explanation: Two independent codes must agree on the SOC magnetic group; a mismatch flags tolerance or input problems.

questions.question: Which canonical variables describe one spin in the joint magnon–phonon model?

options.b: (X, Y) with S⊥ = √S (X x + Y y) and [X, Y] = i
options.c: the angles θ and φ only

questions.explanation: Holstein–Primakoff to linear order: transverse deviations scaled by √S are a canonical pair, like (u, P) for atoms.

questions.question: Why does isotropic exchange striction (G = dJ/dr r̂ 𝟙) not hybridise magnons and phonons in a collinear magnet?

options.b: the linear coupling ∝ x_a·v_b vanishes when all spins are (anti)parallel

questions.explanation: Only non-collinear order (x_a·v_b ≠ 0) or anisotropic/DMI derivatives give terms linear in both u and the magnon.

questions.question: Hands-on: FM chain of tutorial 14 (λ = 6 meV/Å): largest anticrossing gap in meV (2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 1.11 meV where the magnon crosses the longitudinal acoustic phonon.

questions.question: Hands-on: how does the anticrossing gap scale with the magnetoelastic constant λ?
questions.explanation: 0.37, 0.74, 1.11, 1.48 meV for λ = 2, 4, 6, 8 meV/Å: first-order level repulsion, gap ≈ 2|coupling|.

questions.question: In the chain example, which phonon branch hybridises with the magnon?
questions.explanation: Only ∂J/∂d_x (along the chain) is non-zero, so only longitudinal displacements u_x couple.

questions.question: Hands-on: 120° triangular AFM with dJ/dr = 1.5 meV/Å: max |ω − ω_uncoupled| in meV (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 0.033 meV: non-collinear spins make isotropic striction couple linearly.

questions.question: What must phonopy force constants satisfy to be used with --phonons phonopy_params.yaml?

options.b: same primitive cell and atom order as the POSCAR (SymPhase checks it)

questions.explanation: Φ(k) is mapped atom by atom onto the magnetic model; SymPhase refuses a different cell or order.

questions.question: How is the magnon weight of a hybrid mode defined?

options.a: fraction of the energy in spins
options.b: fraction of the symplectic (boson) norm carried by the spin pairs (X, Y)

questions.explanation: For each canonical pair c = −2 Im(q* p); the spin pairs' share of Σc is the magnon weight (1 = pure magnon).

questions.question: What does the quasi-harmonic approximation compute?

options.a: F at the static volume only
options.b: G(T) = min_V [E(V) + F_vib(V, T)] with volume-dependent phonons

questions.explanation: Phonon frequencies depend on V; minimising F over V gives V(T), thermal expansion and G(T).

questions.question: Hands-on: toy Ni (tutorial 15): volumetric thermal expansion β at 300 K in 10⁻⁶/K (1 decimal)?
questions.explanation: β ≈ 38 × 10⁻⁶ /K, i.e. a linear α = β/3 ≈ 12.7 × 10⁻⁶ /K — the right size for Ni.

questions.question: Hands-on: the corresponding LINEAR thermal expansion α at 300 K in 10⁻⁶/K?
questions.explanation: α = β/3 for an isotropic solid.

questions.question: With a Grüneisen parameter γ0 = 0 the quasi-harmonic model gives …

options.b: no thermal expansion: θ_D does not depend on V

questions.explanation: Expansion needs ∂F_vib/∂V ≠ 0, i.e. volume-dependent phonons (β B V = γ C_V).

questions.question: Hands-on: NiAl_qha.csv, harmonic Debye (anh_a removed): stabilisation temperature of Ni3Al-D019 in K?
questions.explanation: 1393 K harmonically; QHA lowers it to 742 K.

questions.question: Hands-on: with quasi-harmonic + anharmonic free energies (vib='qha-debye', anh_a kept): T* of Ni3Al-D019 in K?
questions.explanation: 667 K: the larger Grüneisen parameter and the intrinsic anharmonicity of D019 soften it on heating.

questions.question: In SymPhase's convention F_anh = −(3/2) k_B a T² per atom; what is the anharmonic entropy?
questions.explanation: S = −∂F/∂T = 3 k_B a T, and C_anh = T ∂S/∂T = 3 k_B a T: a > 0 raises the heat capacity linearly in T.
